note.text:
• A height (altitude) goes from a vertex and is perpendicular to the opposite side. The three heights meet at the orthocentre.
• A median joins a vertex to the midpoint of the opposite side. The three medians meet at the centroid (centre of gravity).
• The perpendicular bisector of a side is perpendicular to it at its midpoint. The three meet at the circumcentre, the centre of the circle through the three vertices.
• An angle bisector cuts an angle into two equal angles. The three meet at the incentre, the centre of the circle inside the triangle touching the three sides.

worked_example.problem: In triangle ABC, [AM] is the median from A and BC = {n} cm. Find BM.
steps: A median goes to the midpoint of the opposite side, so M is the midpoint of [BC].

cards.idea: A height is perpendicular to the opposite side; a median goes to its midpoint.
example: The median from A ends at the midpoint of [BC].

cards.idea: The median cuts the opposite side into two equal parts.
example: BC = {n} cm, so BM = MC = {n / 2} cm.

cards.idea: The three lines of each kind meet at one point: orthocentre, centroid, circumcentre, incentre.

check.prompt: Match each set of three lines to the point where they meet.

right.text: A median joins a vertex to the midpoint of the opposite side.
The circumcentre is where the perpendicular bisectors meet.
A height is perpendicular to a side.
An angle bisector cuts an angle into two equal angles.

wrong.text: A median is always perpendicular to the opposite side.
wrong.explain: That is a height; a median goes to the midpoint.

wrong.text: The centroid is where the heights meet.
wrong.explain: The heights meet at the orthocentre; the medians meet at the centroid.

wrong.text: The incentre is the centre of the circle through the three vertices.
wrong.explain: That is the circumcentre; the incentre is the centre of the circle inside the triangle.
